proof:
Source and role. This is Steps 1, 6 and 7 of the parent-supplied proof of the Riesz representation (L¹(μ))* = L^∞(μ), which Simon invokes in Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 2.34 (p. 142). The claim: a bounded linear functional on L¹ that agrees with integration against a bounded density on indicators of measurable sets agrees with it on all integrable functions, because simple functions are dense in L¹.

Hypotheses, for all μ-integrable f, g and all c ∈ ℝ:
- (i) F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g);
- (ii) F(c f) = c F(f);
- (iii) |F(f)| ≤ C ∫|f| dμ;
- θ is measurable with |θ(x)| ≤ M for every x;
- (iv) F(1_A) = ∫_A θ dμ for every measurable A.

1. (Indicators are integrable.) For measurable s ⊆ α, 1_s is measurable and bounded by 1, and μ(α) < ∞, so 1_s is μ-integrable (Lean: (integrable_const 1).indicator hs).

2. (Subtraction.) For integrable f, g we have f − g = f + (−1)·g, where (−1)·g is integrable. By (i) and (ii), F(f − g) = F(f) + (−1) F(g) = F(f) − F(g).

3. (Lipschitz estimate for F.) Put K := max(C, 0) ≥ 0. For integrable f, g, Step 2 and (iii) applied to the integrable function f − g give |F(f) − F(g)| = |F(f − g)| ≤ C ∫|f − g| dμ ≤ K ∫|f − g| dμ, since ∫|f − g| dμ ≥ 0 and C ≤ K.

4. (F respects a.e. equality.) If f, g are integrable and f = g μ-a.e., then |f − g| = 0 μ-a.e., so ∫|f − g| dμ = 0. Step 3 gives |F(f) − F(g)| ≤ 0, hence F(f) = F(g).

5. (Integrability of fθ.) θ is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable (ℝ is second countable), and |θ(x)| ≤ M for all x. So for integrable f, fθ is integrable, with |fθ| ≤ M|f| (Mathlib Integrable.mul_bdd).

6. (Lipschitz estimate for f ↦ ∫ fθ.) Put L := max(M, 0) ≥ 0. For integrable f, g, Step 5 and linearity of the integral give |∫ fθ dμ − ∫ gθ dμ| = |∫ (f − g)θ dμ| ≤ ∫ |f − g| |θ| dμ ≤ ∫ L |f − g| dμ = L ∫|f − g| dμ.

7. (Continuity on L¹.) Let Φ : (α → ℝ) → ℝ and K' ≥ 0 satisfy |Φ(f) − Φ(g)| ≤ K' ∫|f − g| dμ for all integrable f, g. Every u ∈ L¹(μ) (Mathlib α →₁[μ] ℝ) has an integrable representative ⇑u. For u, v ∈ L¹(μ), ⇑(u − v) = ⇑u − ⇑v μ-a.e., so ‖u − v‖_{L¹} = ∫|⇑(u − v)| dμ = ∫|⇑u − ⇑v| dμ (Mathlib L1.norm_eq_integral_norm, Lp.coeFn_sub). Hence |Φ(⇑u) − Φ(⇑v)| ≤ K' ‖u − v‖_{L¹}: the map u ↦ Φ(⇑u) is K'-Lipschitz, in particular continuous, on L¹(μ). By Steps 3 and 6 this applies to Φ = F with K' = K and to Φ = (f ↦ ∫ fθ dμ) with K' = L.

8. (Induction over integrable functions.) Let P(f) be the statement F(f) = ∫ f θ dμ. By the induction principle for integrable functions (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Integrable.induction), P(f) holds for every μ-integrable f once the following four facts are verified.
   (a) Indicators. Let c ∈ ℝ and s be measurable (with μ(s) < ∞). The function x ↦ c·1_s(x) equals c • 1_s, and 1_s is integrable by Step 1. By (ii) and (iv), F(c·1_s) = c F(1_s) = c ∫_s θ dμ = ∫_s cθ dμ = ∫ (c·1_s(x)) θ(x) dμ(x). The last equality holds because (c·1_s(x))θ(x) = 1_s(x)·cθ(x) and ∫ 1_s h dμ = ∫_s h dμ.
   (b) Sums. Let f, g be integrable with P(f) and P(g); the principle also supplies disjoint supports, which is not needed. Since fθ and gθ are integrable (Step 5), (i), P(f), P(g) and additivity of the integral give F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g) = ∫ fθ dμ + ∫ gθ dμ = ∫ (f + g)θ dμ.
   (c) Closedness. The set {u ∈ L¹(μ) : F(⇑u) = ∫ ⇑u θ dμ} is where the two continuous maps u ↦ F(⇑u) and u ↦ ∫ ⇑u θ dμ of Step 7 coincide. It is closed because ℝ is Hausdorff (Mathlib isClosed_eq).
   (d) A.e. congruence. Suppose f = g μ-a.e., f is integrable and P(f) holds. Then g is integrable (Integrable.congr) and F(g) = F(f) by Step 4. Also ∫ gθ dμ = ∫ fθ dμ, because the integrands agree μ-a.e. Hence F(g) = F(f) = ∫ fθ dμ = ∫ gθ dμ, which is P(g).

Therefore F(f) = ∫ f(x) θ(x) dμ(x) for every μ-integrable f. ∎
key_steps: F(f − g) = F f − F g and |F f − F g| ≤ max(C,0) ∫|f − g|, so F(f) = F(g) whenever f = g a.e.
fθ is integrable for integrable f (Integrable.mul_bdd), and |∫ fθ − ∫ gθ| ≤ max(M,0) ∫|f − g|.
u ↦ F(⇑u) and u ↦ ∫ ⇑u θ are Lipschitz, hence continuous, on L¹(μ), since ‖u − v‖ = ∫|⇑u − ⇑v|.

Integrable.induction for P(f): F f = ∫ fθ. Indicators c·1_s follow from homogeneity and the hypothesis, sums from additivity and linearity, closedness from isClosed_eq of continuous maps, and a.e. congruence from Step 1 and integral_congr_ae.
